newsitem.title: UK: UK grain futures jump in active trade.
newsitem.headline: UK grain futures jump in active trade.

text.p: Active short covering helped LIFFE grain futures jump in active trade.
Sterling's fall against other European currencies helped fuel stop loss buying, traders said.
"There was no one single reason why it should have been today," one trader said. "We've been working our way up to this over the past week."
He cited increased optimism on the state of the UK's balance sheet, coupled with France's improved export outlook, notably to Iran.
And a continued lack of supply from farms helped push the market in the right direction, he said.
May dominated wheat volume, with 954 of a total 1,286 lots traded. It last traded 2.50 stg up at 98.00 stg.
Barley also jumped, with active May up 0.75 stg at 94.25. May barley volume was 40 lots of a total 62.
Iran last week bought 300,000 tonnes of European Union soft wheat, mostly French, for shipment in April, European grain traders said on Monday.
Sterling was dragged down by receding expectations of higher UK interest rates in the near future, losing five pfennigs from its day's high against the mark.
